frase_inicial: Michael: your January home choice, retirement at 58 and the cash you need all collide in the same budget

tarjetas.frente: January 2027 home and vacation land together
tarjetas.reverso: If you set money aside for both, your bank cash would be gone. That would make everyday shocks force you to sell investments or borrow instead of keeping plans on track.
tarjetas.detalle: Down payment and one-time costs for home: $113,300 (Michael, Jan 2027); vacation next payment: $3,500 (annual starting Jan 2027).

tarjetas.reverso: Your income and savings likely won’t stretch to the plan’s end age, so without change some planned spending would go unpaid in later life. This is driven by current withdrawals versus what the portfolio can safely supply.
tarjetas.detalle: Projected retirement gap implies needing about $20,231 more per year to close; savings run out at age 85 leaving $32,439 unpaid.

tarjetas.frente: Cash cushion is thinner than you should have
tarjetas.reverso: Right now your accessible cash covers only a few months of essentials. That means a single big bill or income hiccup would push costs onto your credit card or force selling investments.
tarjetas.detalle: Accessible cash today: $30,000 (Michael). Months covered before near-term goals: 3.2 months.

tarjetas.frente: Life and liability protection leave gaps
tarjetas.reverso: Your life cover and lack of extra liability protection mean your income and savings could be exposed if something big happens to you or if a claim exceeds your car or renter cover.
tarjetas.detalle: Life insurance: $180,000 vs recommended $900,000–$1,800,000; umbrella recommended minimum gap: $1,000,000.

tarjetas.frente: Credit card is the most expensive debt
tarjetas.reverso: That card costs the most for each dollar outstanding. Paying it faster reduces interest drain, but it uses the same cash you need for the home and the emergency stash.
tarjetas.detalle: Amex balance: $3,500 at 20%, monthly payment $200, projected payoff July 2028 (Michael).

movimientos.title: Add umbrella cover
movimientos.action: Add $1M of umbrella to raise the liability shield

movimientos.title: Lower the withdrawal rate
movimientos.action: Cutting withdrawals to $10,300/year (6.0%) reaches the sustainable band

movimientos.title: Raise growth allocation toward glide
movimientos.action: Move the invested mix from 74% to 88% growth (glide 98%) for the next horizon-fit band — about $19,900 of the invested book

mapa.aviso: Illustrative simulator: it shows the direction of change, not a Sherpas projection.

siguiente_paso.razon: An extra liability layer protects the cash and savings you’re building for the home and retirement; the plan shows no umbrella and flags this as a clear gap.
pasos: Call your insurer or agent and ask if you have umbrella liability and what it covers
If none, request a quote for at least $1,000,000 in umbrella cover to compare premiums
Decide from the quote whether to buy it now or delay and document the decision
